explanation: L1/N400+ is a word-form detector: it reads a token's surface string, not the word's meaning or grammatical role (token identity explains 57% of its activation variance, position 1%), and it fires on the open-class lexicon of physical specification - lowercase colour terms (green, gray/grey, blue, brown, yellow, red, black, orange, purple, pink, cream), part and geometry nouns (side, centre/center, corner, bottom, left, rim, band, bars, sheet, wall, pieces, halves, branches, bodies, elements, divisions), material, ingredient and measure forms (juice, paste, straw, cord, salt, olive, ice, light, heat, hours, minutes, days, weeks, months, years, degrees, teaspoons, calories, temperature, intensity, '°') and specification/metadata words (option, optional, Details, description, mode, condition, status, errors, labels, stages, margin), plus the procedural particles 'then' and 'off' and the mid-word BPE continuations and non-Latin characters that carry those strings ('ays' in bays/days, 'IDTH' in width, 'ney' in chimney, 'ener' in gardener, 'ison', and single CJK/kana/Cyrillic/Arabic/Thai characters). Membership is by form, not sense: the same form fires in transferred, technical or abstract uses - 'centre' as a verb 0.84 and as a noun 0.84, 'degrees' as academic awards 1.15 and for oven heat 1.46, 'pieces' as musical works 1.24, 'number' in an inventory 1.27, 'green' for 'inexperienced' 0.71 - so no claim is made that a listed form stays quiet in another sense or role; strength is graded by the form and by its neighbours and some occurrences fall below the line ('side' as a verb 0.09, 'bodies' as organisations 0.25, 'bowl' 0.43), and no upcoming token is prepared (the Jacobian lens promotes only replacement-character fragments, kurtosis 43, agreement 20%), so the reading is retrospective. At exactly zero is the determiner/pronoun/auxiliary core (0 of 8,706 determiners active in the scan, and 'the', 'a', 'an', 'and', 'to', 'is', 'are', 'for', 'which', 'who', 'each', 'same' measure 0.00 in every probe); the relational/analytic lexicon (idea, ideas, problem, policy, company, cost, price, work, people, plan, reason, method, theory, argument, question, answer, result, cause, process, knowledge, meaning, purpose, decision, item, detail, example, issue, point, fact, change, difference, relationship, importance, need, help, role) never appears among the scan's 200 highest-mean tokens (cut-off 0.566), and 19 of the 20 abstract sentences I built around it peak at 0.00-0.29 (the exception fires on ' them', not on one of these nouns); class membership is form-specific rather than semantic, so plain object and attribute words that look like class members stay low ('surface', 'cover', 'handle', 'top', 'front', 'inner', 'outer', 'middle', 'panel', 'percent', 'inches', 'meters', 'miles', 'degree', 'table', 'room', 'door', 'tree', 'book', 'map', 'paper', 'water', 'fire', 'rain', 'iron', 'carpet', 'computer' at 0.0-0.55) and so do unobserved colour words ('teal', 'plum', 'slate', 'rose', 'beige' all 0.44). A probe containing at least one listed form is predicted active; a probe of closed-class or relational/analytic text is predicted inactive, but function forms outside the determiner core are not perfectly silent (the scan's POS profile has 125 of 10,566 prepositions and 189 of 11,504 verbs active, about 1-2%, and 'before' and 'than' fire in a minority of their occurrences), so a short probe built only from such forms is not guaranteed negative.
